verdict: OVERFIT — DO NOT USE OLS WEIGHTS FOR PRODUCTION
verdict_reasoning: 1. B) gives w_nn = NEGATIVE (-0.98). OLS thinks NN is anti-predictive. NN-only T188v2 ablation is +51, so NN clearly has signal — OLS is fitting noise.
2. C/D) only 3 of 300 weights nonzero. Real ensemble diversity should give dozens of nonzero weights.

3. Test PnL > Val PnL (288 > 259 in C). Smoking gun. If OLS learned real signal, val should match test or be higher. Test being higher means the noise pattern the 3 LGB models memorized happened to align with both val (80-95) and test (96-119) — pure in-sample artifact.
4. D) Lasso α=1e-5 zeros ALL weights. No signal is robust to even tiny L1 regularization.

comparison_to_known_baselines.T192_OLS_platform: predicted to be < 30 (likely much worse than simple mean)

recommendation: KILL the per-model OLS weighting direction. To find signal that actually generalizes OOD: (1) use walk-forward validation where val period is OUTSIDE training period (e.g., train on 0-95, val on 96-119, test on 120+ — but that requires re-training); (2) constrain OLS solution space: sum_w=1 + each w_i >= 1/N (forces honest averaging); (3) test on simulated platform-style OOD (date 120+ data only)
